data.exact_reserve_text: Some niche lines, particularly Aviation and Political Risk, have seen significant loss experience in the period, and whilst in general prior year reserves continue to hold up well there have been two very specific accounts that have required reserve strengthening. Recognition of the Talisman claim, an emergence of a loss attaching to an historic Year of Account, has been required in the period. However, increased notifications on the New Zealand earthquake claims have required strengthening of reserves on prior years, leading to a more modest (but still better than plan) 87% combined ratio for the year. Healthcare and Professional Indemnity ("PI") - particularly the UK Solicitors' Professional Indemnity account, which has required some additional reserve strengthening on the older Years of Account - have proven more problematic.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reported that favourable current accident year performance was offset by backyear reserve strengthening. Specific prioryear strengthening was required due to the emergence of the Talisman claim, increased notifications on New Zealand earthquake claims and additional strengthening on older Professional Indemnity (UK Solicitors) exposures. These prioryear deteriorations reduced the benefit of a generally strong Marine, Aviation & Transport division and led the Board to describe the overall prioryear movement as an adverse adjustment to reserves.

data.data_quality_notes: No prior-year comparative column for gross 'Claims outstanding' was provided in the Balance Sheet; therefore opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January is not available and has been set to null. No explicit GROSS prioryear reserve movement figure is provided in the notes or narrative; only qualitative descriptions of reserve strengthening are given (gross prior year development not quantified). Premiums and statement figures in the accounts are presented in GBP 000 in source documents and have been converted to millions here.
